biomarkers.name: IDH1 / IDH2 wildtype
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes from IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma; worse prognosis

biomarkers.name: MGMT promoter methylation
biomarkers.clinical_use: Predicts benefit from temozolomide and is prognostic (better outcome); informs treatment selection, especially in elderly/frail patients

biomarkers.name: TERT promoter mutations (C228T, C250T)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic criterion in molecular GBM (with wildtype IDH and other features)

biomarkers.name: EGFR amplification
biomarkers.clinical_use: Molecular criterion for GBM; EGFR-directed therapies/ADCs have been investigated in trials (including depatuxizumab-mafodotin, development discontinued)

biomarkers.name: EGFRvIII
biomarkers.clinical_use: Rindopepimut vaccine failed; CAR-T and other EGFRvIII-directed trials ongoing

biomarkers.name: H3 K27M / H3 G34
biomarkers.prevalence: Rare in adult GBM (defines separate entities)
biomarkers.clinical_use: H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma and H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma are separate entities in WHO CNS5

biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E
biomarkers.prevalence: Rare in GBM (~1-3%); enriched in epithelioid GBM and some younger patients
biomarkers.clinical_use: BRAF/MEK inhibition (for example dabrafenib + trametinib) may be used in BRAF V600E-mutant high-grade glioma

biomarkers.name: MSI / dMMR + TMB
biomarkers.prevalence: Rare de novo; hypermutation may emerge after temozolomide, but this is often not MSI/dMMR-driven
biomarkers.clinical_use: Checkpoint inhibitor benefit is established for MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high tissue-agnostic indications, but benefit in glioblastoma is limited/inconsistent; consider testing in select recurrent cases

biomarkers.name: PDGFRA amplification / mutation
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent hallmark driver alteration in a subset of IDH-wildtype GBM; may support biologic subclassification and eligibility for targeted trials

biomarkers.name: CDKN2A / CDKN2B homozygous deletion
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common cooperating alteration in IDH-wildtype GBM; not a standalone WHO molecular criterion for GBM, but part of the characteristic genomic profile

biomarkers.name: PTEN loss / mutation
biomarkers.clinical_use: Frequent PI3K/AKT pathway alteration in IDH-wildtype GBM; mainly biologic relevance and trial stratification rather than routine standard-of-care selection

biomarkers.name: NF1 alteration
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associated with mesenchymal transcriptional state/subtype; mainly biologic and subclassification relevance

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Diffuse infiltrating high-grade astrocytic tumour with microvascular proliferation and/or necrosis (pseudopalisading necrosis characteristic)
variants: epithelioid GBM (BRAF V600E in a subset)

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Classic 'cold' 1 sparse T cells, extensive tumour-associated microglia and macrophages, immune-suppressive; blood-brain barrier and local CNS immune context limit immune access
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Microvascular proliferation (glomeruloid) and pseudopalisading necrosis are characteristic histologic features; extensive infiltration into surrounding brain

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Likely arises from neural stem/progenitor cells or glial progenitors; the subventricular zone (SVZ) has been implicated in some cases, and astrocyte-like glioma stem cells (GSCs) sustain tumour
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: TCGA transcriptomic subtypes reflect distinct lineage states: proneural (often OPC-like, commonly PDGFRA-altered), classical (astrocyte-like, EGFR-amplified), mesenchymal (associated with NF1 alteration); recurrent tumours often shift toward mesenchymal state
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Glioma stem cell (GSC) hierarchy with cellular heterogeneity 1 subpopulations occupy distinct lineage states (neural progenitor-like, oligodendrocyte progenitor-like, astrocyte-like, mesenchymal-like) that interconvert; state transitions after therapy drive resistance
